phd-defence-10-september-2026/0.say: Over the past three years, I've studied why symptoms can persist after concussion when routine imaging offers little explanation. One way to understand a system is to perturb it: make a controlled change and watch what follows. We used two different probes. A magnetic contrast agent changes the MRI signal, allowing us to follow its passage through the brain. In a separate experiment, we lower the oxygen people breathe and measure the physiological response. Together, these approaches examine blood-tissue exchange and oxygen use.

acute-to-persistent-symptoms/3.say: Many people improve over the following days and weeks. Others continue to struggle. Headache may persist, while fatigue, poor concentration, disturbed sleep or changes in mood become more noticeable. For the adults we studied, this had often continued for years. These symptoms affect everyday life, but they don't tell us which biological process is responsible. That is the problem behind the thesis.

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/0.say: Let's return to our runner. MRI reconstructs the brain from signals produced by hydrogen nuclei, largely in water and fat. Radiofrequency pulses excite the nuclei, and magnetic-field gradients encode where the signals come from. The contrast agent changes how nearby water responds to MRI, so repeated images let us follow its passage.

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/3.say: The contrast agent is gadobutrol, a gadolinium chelate. It changes the relaxation of nearby water protons, producing enhancement in our T one-weighted acquisition. We inject it through a vein in the arm; it passes through the heart and lungs before reaching the brain's arteries.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/3.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/3.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/4.say: Watch the first passage as the bolus reaches the brain.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/4.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/4.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/5.say: The blood passes from arteries into smaller vessels, through the vascular bed, and out through the veins. Most contrast follows that route. A small amount crossing into tissue would behave differently, which gives us something to measure.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/5.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/5.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/6.say: This is a real dynamic acquisition from a participant I scanned. The signal brightens as contrast arrives. We used two boluses, so there are two main passages. At every location, we record how the signal changes over time.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/6.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/6.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/7.say: Each three-dimensional image is divided into voxels, the volume equivalent of pixels. A voxel contributes one signal value at each time point, combining everything within that small volume.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/7.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/7.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/8.say: Let's select a voxel in the cortex and look at what lies inside it.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/8.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/8.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/9.say: This anatomy comes from the H zero one reconstruction of human cortex. A surgical specimen was preserved, imaged by serial electron microscopy, and reconstructed in three dimensions. The anatomy is real; the physiological processes I animate on it are illustrations.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/9.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/9.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/10.say: Both excitatory and inhibitory neurons fire electrical impulses. Sodium and potassium flowing through channels generate the electrical wave along the axon. At most synapses, calcium entry triggers chemical messenger release. These messengers can make the next neuron more or less likely to fire. Maintaining the ion gradients needed for this signalling costs energy.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/10.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/10.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/11.say: Blood supplies the oxygen and glucose that support this energy demand. Signals between neurons, glia and vascular cells help adjust local blood flow as activity changes. This link between neural activity and blood supply is called neurovascular coupling.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/11.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/11.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/12.say: Vessel-associated cells support and regulate the circulation. Pericytes contribute, although this particular reconstructed segment is not independently identified as one. Their effects on calibre depend on their position and type.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/12.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/12.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/13.say: Microglia survey tissue with fine processes, respond to injury and clear damaged material. They can support repair or contribute to injury, depending on the response and its duration.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/13.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/13.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/14.say: Oligodendrocytes form myelin, helping signals travel efficiently along axons while also supporting them metabolically.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/14.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/14.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/15.say: Astrocytes keep the environment around neurons stable, clearing neurotransmitters and regulating potassium. They also use calcium signals within the cell, which can contribute to blood-flow regulation. Their endfeet contact vessels and help maintain the specialised endothelial lining that forms the blood-brain barrier.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/15.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/15.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/16.say: Here we illustrate contrast passing through a vessel, with a small amount crossing into the surrounding space. An intact blood-brain barrier strongly restricts this agent. The animation shows what escape and diffusion could look like; it does not measure leakage in this specimen.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/16.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/16.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/17.say: The escaped tracer occupies the space between cells. Some can remain while vascular contrast washes out, and a second bolus adds another contribution. Accumulation depends on delivery, transfer and return, rather than on one property of the vessel alone.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/17.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/17.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/18.say: At the scanner's scale, all of this is combined within a voxel. We cannot watch individual molecules cross a capillary. We infer their behaviour from the changing signal.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/18.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/18.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/19.say: We first convert that signal to an estimated concentration, using the acquisition settings and baseline relaxation measurements. This gives the tissue concentration curve, C T. Its peaks and later values contain vascular and possible extravascular contributions. A late tail alone is not proof of leakage.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/19.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/19.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-i-bolus-to-voxel/20.say: A voxel in a supplying artery gives us an input curve, C A. Comparing the input with the tissue response lets us ask what happened during passage through the tissue. I'll use simplified curves to explain the model, then return to the measurements.
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/20.title: p-Brain
study-i-bolus-to-voxel/20.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/0.say: Imagine the input passed through unchanged. The tissue curve would be identical. We can build the actual response one contribution at a time.
input-to-tissue-patlak/0.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/0.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/1.say: Blood follows paths with different transit times, delaying and broadening the response. The branching diagram illustrates this distribution of passage times.
input-to-tissue-patlak/1.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/1.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/2.say: A convolution describes this mixing: delayed copies of the input, added with different weights. This transit kernel builds intuition; it is not fitted in our Patlak analysis. There is also a volume effect. Only a small fraction of a tissue voxel is blood. Averaging its tracer concentration over the whole voxel reduces the height of the curve.
input-to-tissue-patlak/2.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/2.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/3.say: If some tracer crosses into tissue and remains during the measurement, successive arrivals add to what is already there. This produces a slower accumulating contribution alongside the vascular passage.
input-to-tissue-patlak/3.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/3.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/4.say: The yellow component follows the current input concentration, scaled by epsilon one. The orange tissue curve already contains this contribution.
input-to-tissue-patlak/4.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/4.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/5.say: The purple component depends on accumulated input, scaled by epsilon two. Yellow and purple give the orange curve. We want to estimate these two unknown coefficients.
input-to-tissue-patlak/5.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/5.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/6.say: Divide every term by the input concentration at that time.
input-to-tissue-patlak/6.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/6.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/7.say: In the first term the input cancels. The other term becomes accumulated input divided by current input, multiplied by epsilon two. Keep the original expression in view. On the left is the tissue concentration divided by the current input. On the right, the integral is also divided by the current input. We can give these two ratios simpler names.
input-to-tissue-patlak/7.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/7.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/9.say: Each measurement becomes a point in these coordinates. Early points can curve away from a line because transit and mixing remain important.
input-to-tissue-patlak/9.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/9.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/10.say: We fit an appropriate late window, where the rapidly exchanging contribution has a stable relationship with the input. Patlak also assumes negligible return of accumulated tracer during that window. A straight-looking fit does not remove the need to check those assumptions.
input-to-tissue-patlak/10.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/10.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/11.say: The slope is epsilon two. A steeper slope indicates more accumulation relative to the delivered tracer. That converts the slowly changing part of the tissue curve into a parameter.
input-to-tissue-patlak/11.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/11.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/12.say: The intercept is epsilon one, found by extending the fitted line to the vertical axis. It estimates the size of the rapidly reversible contribution under the model's concentration convention.
input-to-tissue-patlak/12.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/12.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

input-to-tissue-patlak/13.say: For our analysis, the slope gives K eye, the net influx constant, and the intercept gives V B, the apparent vascular volume. Higher K eye is consistent with greater tracer transfer, but is not a direct measurement of one vessel wall's permeability. In the production analysis we used a sinus-derived effective input, shifted to carotid arrival, with consistent blood and concentration conventions.
input-to-tissue-patlak/13.title: input-to-tissue-patlak
input-to-tissue-patlak/13.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-iii-capillary-oxygen/1.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-iii-capillary-oxygen/2.say: We cannot measure this for each tiny vessel with our protocol. Instead, we estimate the balance globally using the large vessels supplying and draining the brain. That is an MRI implementation of the Fick principle.
study-iii-capillary-oxygen/2.title: Measurement model
study-iii-capillary-oxygen/2.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-iii-fick-brain/0.say: The estimate combines three measurements and an assumption about haemoglobin. We can build it one term at a time.

study-iii-fick-brain/1.say: The pulse oximeter on the finger measures peripheral saturation, S P O two. We use it as an estimate of arterial saturation, S A O two.
study-iii-fick-brain/1.title: study-iii-fick-brain
study-iii-fick-brain/1.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-iii-fick-brain/2.say: Susceptibility-based oximetry estimates venous saturation in the superior sagittal sinus, using the magnetic difference between oxygenated and deoxygenated haemoglobin. Subtracting venous from arterial saturation gives the saturation drop across the circulation. Combined with haemoglobin concentration, this estimates the oxygen content removed from each unit of blood.
study-iii-fick-brain/2.title: study-iii-fick-brain
study-iii-fick-brain/2.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-iii-fick-brain/3.say: Phase-contrast MRI measures inflow through the two internal carotid arteries and the basilar artery. We normalise their total flow to brain mass and combine it with haemoglobin concentration. In this study haemoglobin was a fixed population value, rather than an individual blood measurement.
study-iii-fick-brain/3.title: study-iii-fick-brain
study-iii-fick-brain/3.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-iii-fick-brain/4.say: The product is C M R O two: the cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen. It estimates oxygen use from flow and the arterial-venous difference. Haemoglobin is expressed in oxygen-binding units, and saturations enter as fractions. The sinus measurement is a proxy for venous oxygenation, so this remains a global estimate with assumptions.
study-iii-fick-brain/4.title: study-iii-fick-brain
study-iii-fick-brain/4.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

study-iii-fick-brain/5.say: After measuring at normoxia, we lower the oxygen in the inspired gas through a controlled delivery system and face mask. We aim for a saturation of approximately eighty percent. This challenges the brain to compensate for reduced oxygen availability, while we measure flow and oxygen use again.
study-iii-fick-brain/5.title: study-iii-fick-brain
study-iii-fick-brain/5.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

a-controlled-descent-not-a-binary-condit.say: This trace shows the measured fall in saturation. The central line represents the cohort median, with bands showing variation between participants. The target and achieved saturation are different quantities. The analysis models the repeated measurements against each participant's achieved saturation and tests whether that relationship differs between groups. This accounts for differences in challenge size, but not every influence on physiology. Ventilation and carbon dioxide can also change during hypoxia, and the measurements depend on the timing and stability of the gas exposure.

was-the-deficit-delivery-or-oxygen-use/0.say: Start with the top row. Resting global blood flow did not show a significant group difference. Both groups increased flow during hypoxia, and we did not detect a difference in that response. In the middle row, resting oxygen consumption was lower in patients. The age- and sex-adjusted difference was about seventeen micromoles per hundred grams per minute, approximately twelve percent of the control mean. During hypoxia, patients also showed a greater fall in oxygen consumption relative to their desaturation. The bottom row adds a regional measurement: lactate from spectroscopy in the precuneus. Lactate reflects the balance of production, oxidation and transport; it is not a specific marker of oxygen running out. We found no significant group difference at rest or in reactivity, with fewer controls contributing to spectroscopy. These results point to a difference in global oxygen use, without establishing whether the cause lies in exchange, cellular metabolism or demand. A similar bulk blood-flow response does not prove that capillary oxygen delivery or neurovascular coupling is normal.
was-the-deficit-delivery-or-oxygen-use/0.title: Physiological results
was-the-deficit-delivery-or-oxygen-use/0.source: Reviewed Voice.m4a rehearsal; substantive corrections documented in phd_voice_review_2026-09-07

did-lower-oxygen-use-track-pulse-intoler.say: We also examined differences within the patient group using the symptom-limited bike test. Exercise intolerance was associated with lower resting oxygen consumption, with an adjusted difference of about twenty micromoles per hundred grams per minute. We did not detect a subgroup difference in oxygen-metabolism reactivity. This was a secondary, uncorrected comparison that needs confirmation. The association does not establish whether reduced oxygen use contributes to exercise intolerance, or whether both reflect a shared upstream process. It also does not diagnose an autonomic disorder.
